questions.question: Find the length of a diagonal of a cuboid whose dimensions are 12 m, 10 m and 8 m. (up to one decimal point)
questions.solution:
Given:

Length = 12 m

Breadth = 10 m

Height = 8 m

Formula Used:

Diagonal of cuboid = √(Length)2 + (Breadth)2 + (Height)2

Calculation:

Diagonal of cuboid = √(Length)² + (Breadth)² + (Height)²

⇒ Diagonal of cuboid = √(12)² + (10)² + (8)²

⇒ Diagonal of cuboid = √(144 + 100 + 64)

⇒ √308 = 17.54

**The length of a diagonal of a cuboid is 17.54 m.**

questions.question: In Class I, there are 12 students of average age 20 years and in Class II, there are 16 students of average age 23 years. What will be the approximate average age for all the students of these two classes?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Class I: No. of students = 12, Average age = 20 years

Class II: No. of students = 16, Average age = 23 years

**Formula used:**

Average = Sum of all observations/Total no. of observation

**Calculation:**

Total age of the students of Class I = 12 × 20 = 240 years

Total age of the students of Class II = 16 × 23 = 368 years

Average age = (240 + 368)/2

⇒ 608/(12 + 16) = 608/28 = 21.71 ≈ 21.7 years

**∴ Approximate average age for all the students of these two classes is 21.7 years.**

questions.question: The mean weight of 32 students in a school is 50 kg. If the weight of the teacher be included, the mean rises by 500 grams. Find the weight of the teacher.
questions.solution:
Given: 

The average weight of 32 students in a school is 50 kg.

If the age of the teacher is also included, the average weight increases by 500 grams = 50 + 0.5 = 50.5

Concept Used:

Average Value = (Sum of all the values)/(Total values)

Calculations:

According to the question,

Let the weight of the teacher be T, then

Average weight = (32 × 50 + T)/33

⇒ 50.5 = (32 × 50 + T)/33 

⇒ 50.5 × 33 = 1600 + T 

⇒ T = 1666.5 - 1600 = 66.5 kg

∴ The weight of the teacher is 66.5 kg.

questions.question: If 20% of a number is subtracted from a second number and the second number decreases to its 70%, then what is the ratio of the first number to the second number?
questions.solution:
Given:

20% of a number is subtracted from a second number and the second number decreases to its 70%

Calculations:

Let the first and second numbers be x and y, respectively.

y - 20% of x = y * 70/100

⇒ y + 1/5x = 7/10y

⇒ 3/10y = 1/5x

⇒ x : y = 3 : 2

**The ratio of the first number to the second number is 3 : 2.**

questions.question: The sum of two numbers 10373 + 24871 is divisible by:
questions.solution:
Concept used:

Divisibility law of 6 ⇒ A number is divisible by 6 if the sum of its digit is divisible by 3 and the last digit is even.

Divisibility law of 7: Take the last digit of the number, double it Then subtract the result from the rest of the number If the resulting number is evenly divisible by 7

If the last three digits of a number are divisible by 8, then the number is completely divisible by 8.

The divisibility rule of 13 states that: Add the unit place digit after multiplication with 4 to the remaining number to the left of the digit at units place. If the result of the addition is divisible by 13, then the complete number is also divisible by 13.

**Calculation**

⇒ 10373 + 24871 = 35244

Option 1:

⇒ 35244 - 4 × 2 = 35236 ⇒ 35236 - 4 × 6 = 35212

35212 is not divisible by 7, so 35244 is also not divisible by 7.

Option 2:

last three digits of the number i.e. 244 is not divisible by 8, hence 35244 is also not divisible by 8.

Option 3:

⇒ 3 + 5 + 2 + 4 + 4 = 18

The sum of its digit is divisible by 3 and the last digit is even, hence number is divisible by 6.

Option 4:

⇒ 35244 + 4 × 4 = 3540 

3540 is not divisible by 13, so 3540 is also not divisible by 13.

**The answer is option 3.**

⇒ SP of 1000gm rice = 1130x/760 = 1.569x

Now P% = [(1.486x - x)/x] × 100

⇒ P% = 0.486 × 100 = 48.6%

questions.question: The internal and external diameters of a hollow hemispherical bowl are 6 cm and 10 cm, respectively. If it is melted and recast into a solid cylinder of diameter 14 cm, what is the height of the cylinder in cm?
questions.solution:
Given:

The internal and external diameters of a hollow hemispherical bowl are 6 cm and 10 cm

Concept used:

The volume of a hollow hemisphere = The volume of a solid cylinder (Where R is the radius)

The volume of a hollow hemisphere = 2/3π(R³ - r³) (Where R is the radius)

Radius = Diameter ÷ 2

The volume of a solid cylinder = πr²h

Calculation:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/5d688739f1f5ab5a57eb2ab9c394736ccc4676ea31c9af3f4213696606ac8edf.png] 

The volume of a hollow hemisphere = 2/3π(R3 - r3)

⇒ 2/3 × π × (53 - 33)

⇒ 2/3 × π × 98

The volume of a solid cylinder = πr2h

⇒ πr2h = π72h 

⇒ 2/3 × π × 98 = π × 7² × h

⇒ h = 4/3

⇒ h = 1.33

**The height of the cylinder in cm is 1.33.**

questions.question: Which of the following numbers is NOT divisible by 72?
questions.solution:
**Concept used:**

Divisibility rule of 8 is the last three digits of a number divisible by 8.

Divisibility of 9 is the sum of all the digits of a number divisible by 9.

**Calculation:**

72 = 8 × 9

Considering option (1) 359784,

⇒ 784 is divisible by 8.

⇒ (3 + 5 + 9 + 7 + 8 + 4) = 36 is divisible by 9.

So, it is divisible by 72.

Considering option (2) 426816,

⇒ 816 is divisible by 8.

⇒ (4 + 2 + 6 + 8 + 1 + 6) = 27 is divisible by 9.

So, it is divisible by 72.

Considering option (3) 486280,

⇒ 280 is divisible by 8.

⇒ (4 + 8 + 6 + 2 + 8 + 0) = 28 is not divisible by 9.

So, it is not divisible by 72.

Considering option (4) 754344,

⇒ 344 is divisible by 8.

⇒ (7 + 5 + 4 + 3 + 4 + 4) = 27 is divisible by 9.

So, it is divisible by 72.

**∴ Option 3 is NOT divisible by 72. **

questions.question: In a circular race along a track of length 3600 m, X and Y run at speeds of 27 km/h and 45 km/h, respectively. Suppose they start at the same time and in the same direction, when will they meet again at the starting point?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Speed X = 27 × 5/18 = 7.5 m/s; Speed Y = 45 × 5/18 = 12.5 m/s.

Time for X to complete 1 lap = 3600 ÷ 7.5 = 480 sec.

Time for Y to complete 1 lap = 3600 ÷ 12.5 = 288 sec.

Meeting time at starting point = LCM(480, 288).

LCM(480, 288) = 1440 sec.

**∴ The correct answer is 1440 sec.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Track Length = 3600 m

Speed of X = 27 km/h

Speed of Y = 45 km/h

**Formula Used:**

Time = Distance ÷ Speed

Time to meet at starting point = LCM(Time taken by X for one lap, Time taken by Y for one lap)

 
 
• 
 START
 

 X (27 km/h)
 

 Y (45 km/h)
 Track: 3600 m
 Meeting at Start = LCM(TX, TY)

**Calculations:**

⇒ Speed of X in m/s = 27 × (5/18) = 7.5 m/s

⇒ Speed of Y in m/s = 45 × (5/18) = 12.5 m/s

⇒ Time taken by X (TX) = 3600 ÷ 7.5 = 480 sec

⇒ Time taken by Y (TY) = 3600 ÷ 12.5 = 288 sec

⇒ Required time = LCM(480, 288)

⇒ 480 = 2⁵ × 3 × 5

⇒ 288 = 2⁵ × 3²

⇒ LCM = 2⁵ × 3² × 5 = 32 × 9 × 5 = 1440 sec

**∴ The correct answer is 1440 sec.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Meeting Anywhere on Track

To find the first time they meet anywhere on the track, use Time = Track Length ÷ Relative Speed. Same direction: Relative Speed = S₁ − S₂. Opposite direction: Relative Speed = S₁ + S₂.

Unit Conversion

To convert speed from km/h to m/s, multiply by 5/18. To convert m/s to km/h, multiply by 18/5.

LCM of Fractions

If lap times are in fractions, LCM(a/b, c/d) = LCM(a, c) ÷ HCF(b, d).</p

questions.question: The students in three batches of a dance class are in ratio 2 : 3 : 5. If 20 students increase in each batch the ratio changes to 4 : 5 : 7. Find the total number of students in the three batches before the increase.
questions.solution:
**Calculation**

Ratio of students in three batches = 2x : 3x : 5x

According to the question,

(2x + 20) : (3x + 20) : (5x + 20) = 4 : 5 : 7

∴ Comparing the two ratios,

(2x + 20) / (3x + 20) = 4/5

⇒ x = 10

The initial number of students are = (2 × 10), ( 3 × 10), (5 × 10) = 20, 30, 50

Total Number of students = 20 + 30 + 50 = 100

**The total number of students in the three batches before the increase is 100.**

questions.question: If the cost price is 94% of the selling price, then find the profit percentage.
questions.solution:
Given:

The cost price is 94% of the selling price

Formula Used:

Profit = S.P. - C.P.

Profit % = Profit/C.P. × 100

Calculations:

Let the Selling Price is 100x.

Then the Cost price = 94% of 100x

= 94x

⇒ Profit = 100x - 94x = 6x

⇒ Profit % = (6x/94x) × 100

⇒ Profit % = 6.4%

**∴ The profit percentage is 6.4%.**
